title: Python: EventSandbox ergonomic shim for streaming chat + idempotent retry cookbook
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Introduce a compact, testable shim (EventSandbox) for the Python SDK that unifies event-first and chunk-first streaming patterns, makes retries idempotent and resumable, and provides a low-friction migration path for existing integrators.
background: Users building streaming chat integrations face several ergonomic problems: mixing low-level SSE/HTTP chunks with semantic events, awkward retry semantics when partial events have been emitted to callers, and brittle backpressure interfaces. Existing internal patterns are fragmented across several tickets and example apps. We need a small, focused helper in the SDK that codifies best practices and can be used by product code and customer apps.
proposal: Add EventSandbox: a lightweight in-process harness and public shim with these properties: 1) event-first API: callers receive typed events (token, delta, end, error, meta) rather than raw chunks; 2) checkpointable stream cursor: SDK emits monotonic cursors so clients can persist/resume; 3) idempotent replay: the shim can replay buffered events to new consumers without duplicating side-effects; 4) declarative retry rules: policy DSL (retry-on-network, retry-on-early-cancel) that uses cursor to resume; 5) ergonomic hooks: on_event, on_error, on_checkpoint, and transform pipelines for compact user code; 6) test harness: a sandbox mode that can inject synthetic network delays, partial fragments, and out-of-order events for deterministic unit tests.
acceptance_criteria: EventSandbox API documented in SDK docs with at least two examples (basic echo stream, resumable chat consumer)
Unit tests cover: fragment reassembly, cursor resume, idempotent replay, and retry policies (>= 90% coverage for core shim)
A migration guide exists that converts one reference app from chunk-first to event-first with <= 10 LOC change in consumer code
Performance overhead under load < 5% token throughput compared to baseline raw stream path (measured in dedicated bench)
Telemetry: emits events for retry attempts, resumed sessions, and dropped/ignored duplicate events
tasks: Design API surface and produce a one-pager with sequence diagrams
Implement EventSandbox core: parser, cursor, replay buffer, transform hooks
Add retry policy DSL and integrate with existing request/transport layer
Write unit and integration tests including deterministic sandbox scenarios
Benchmark end-to-end throughput and latency; compare against current streaming path
Author docs + migration guide + two example snippets (consumer, server-sim)
Code review and address SDK lint/security checks
Ship behind a feature flag; run dogfood on one internal service for 2 weeks
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with DX and Runtime teams. Alignment on cursor shape (string opaque token) and minimal metadata payload (offset, model, prompt-hash).
2026-02-18: Prototype parser completed (handles token/role/meta fragments + partial JSON toolcalls). Logged early bug: out-of-order meta events when connection retries mid-chunk.
2026-02-24: Added monotonic checkpoint cursor; initial replay buffer uses time-bounded retention (default 60s) to bound memory. Open question: should retention be size-based instead?

2026-03-01: First PR opened against py-sdk feature/event-sandbox (#4021). Initial review: reviewers ask for clearer error semantics when cursor is unknown on resume. Action: add RetryPolicy option 'fail_on_unknown_cursor'.

2026-03-05: Benchmarks show ~2.3% additional CPU for parser+replay under 200RPS workload. Memory repro shows replay buffer spikes in pathological long-running sessions (>10min); plan to add configurable max_buffer_bytes and auto-eviction.

2026-03-08: UX review with Developer Advocates: requested a high-level convenience helper .stream_consumer(...) that wires on_event hooks and returns an async context manager. Will prototype in separate PR.
2026-03-10: Integration tests added for resumable retry (network disconnect at token 312). Tests pass locally. Preparing merge-ready PR after addressing lint failures.
testing_plan: Unit tests for parser and replay buffer (parametrized for partial fragments). Integration tests simulate disconnects at many offsets and assert no duplicate side-effects when replaying. Sandbox harness will produce deterministic streams for CI. Add e2e dogfood job that runs internal chat service against staging for 14 days and tracks resume success rate and retry counts.
rollout_plan: Feature flagged behind 'event_sandbox' boolean. Canary rollout: enable for internal-dev team, then for 2 small customers on dedicated capacity, monitor errors/retries for 48h, then gradual ramp to GA. Provide opt-out path (use raw chunk stream) for customers who rely on previous behavior.
notes: Cursor design must remain forward-compatible if we add partition or shard fields later; use opaque base64 encoded JSON
We intentionally keep the initial API minimal: prefer small helpers to full-blown state machines
Avoid coupling EventSandbox to a particular transport; it should accept an async iterator of bytes/chunks
Consider future support for non-chat streaming (embeddings, rerank logs) if event model generalizes
open_questions: Retention model for replay buffer: time-based vs size-based vs event-count?
Should the SDK expose a 'commit' API for clients to acknowledge durable side-effects, or keep that responsibility on callers?
What is the canonical error surface for 'cursor unknown' vs 'cursor expired' to make retries debuggable?
